structure: Part 2, What are you importing. Read the 'what are you importing' and 'germinal products: section 1' describes of about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js and the 'what are you importing' describe (S06 to S08) of snagging.fit.spec.js, then opened and mined all 9 trace zips the part names: (1) renders the commodity search for live animals, 59 actions; (2) nothing selected is an error, 48 actions; (3) search lists the species of a commodity, ticking one adds it, 60 actions; (4) several commodities selected together and cleared, 59 actions; (5) save and return to overview, 38 actions; (6) germinal commodity search: semen, ova and embryos, 102 actions; (7) S06 inset under the heading, 40 actions; (8) S07 search box hint, 51 actions, with a second no-JavaScript context; (9) S08 searching and ticking species, 100 actions, with two no-JavaScript contexts. Every trace reaches one page, /design-release-2.1/what-are-you-importing, after the notification type page and the origin page (part 1's). It has a live-animals variant (reached after choosing live animals on the notification type page) and a germinal-products variant (reached from /create-notification?category=germinal-products), which differ in the search hint and the catalogue they search. Page states mined: default; Help with commodity codes open; nothing-selected error (POST answered 200 with the page re-rendered); search results open for 'cattle', 'horse', 'pig', '0101', 'Bos' (live) and 'semen', 'embryo' (germinal); one and two species selected; Clear all; Save and return to overview (POST 302 to /notification-hub); Save and continue with a germinal selection (POST 302 to /reason-for-import); and the page without JavaScript, blank and with 'cattle' typed. The search, results list, selection panel and chips are custom app-commodity-search markup over govuk-checkboxes; the rest of the page is govuk-inset-text, govuk-details, govuk-button and govuk-error-summary. Claims about which commodities and species the catalogue holds are recorded as what the prototype rendered, which the goal says is demo data. Snapshot pointers: trace (1) actions 36 and 46, (2) 35, (3) 35 and 47, (4) 26, 32, 44 and 46, (6) 24, 36, 56, 70 and 86, (7) 27, (8) 35, (9) 42, 56, 64 and 82. Refs name each trace by its zip file name.

claims.statement: Without JavaScript the page renders the heading, inset, label, hint, an empty search box, the Search button, the Help with commodity codes expander and both submit buttons, but no results list and no tick boxes.

Without JavaScript, typing 'cattle' into the search box shows no results, and the Search button is type=button, so it submits nothing: a user without JavaScript cannot choose a commodity on this page.

claims.note: That nothing can be chosen is inferred from the empty results, the type=button Search button and the absence of any noscript fallback (NOSCRIPT=0). The goal requires every page to work without JavaScript.

The page uses GOV.UK Frontend for the inset text, details, buttons, error summary, error message, tag, back link and the species checkboxes, and custom classes for the page header, status line, commodity search, results, selected panel, chips and the button group (app-origin-form-actions).
